chief_complaint: new severe headache, scalp tenderness, and jaw pain when chewing
hpi_details: 75F presents with a 2-week history of a constant right-sided temporal headache. She notes it hurts to brush her hair. When she eats steak, her jaw gets very tired and painful. She also had an episode of brief vision loss in her right eye yesterday.

investigation_events.title: STAT inflammatory-marker results
investigation_events.availability_message: The STAT inflammatory markers are now available; threatened vision requires treatment without waiting for imaging or biopsy.

core_concepts: Large vessel vasculitis affecting branches of the carotid artery, predominantly in older adults.
Jaw claudication and amaurosis fugax (vision loss) are highly specific.
common_misconceptions: Waiting for temporal artery biopsy results before starting steroids.
dangerous_errors: Delaying high-dose corticosteroids, leading to permanent irreversible blindness.
management_principles: Start high-dose corticosteroids immediately if suspected, before biopsy; use intravenous methylprednisolone when there is threatened or established visual loss. Check ESR/CRP.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Clinical Guidance

reference_soap.subjective: 75F with new temporal headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, and amaurosis fugax.
reference_soap.objective: Right temporal artery is prominent, firm, and tender. No pulses on the right.
reference_soap.plan: STAT ESR and CRP. Because she has transient visual loss, start intravenous methylprednisolone immediately to prevent permanent blindness. Arrange urgent temporal artery biopsy.

learning_objectives: Identify the signs of GCA and understand the critical need for immediate steroid therapy.

teaching.one_liner: An elderly female with temporal headache, jaw claudication, and vision changes requiring emergent steroids.

must_ask.say: Is the headache on one side, and does it hurt to touch your scalp?
Does your jaw get tired or painful when you chew, like when eating meat?
Have you had any episodes of blurred vision or vision loss?
Have you had any aching or stiffness in your shoulders or hips?
When did the headache start, and when did the vision loss happen?

history.answer: I've developed this severe, throbbing headache on the right side of my head over the past two weeks, and it hurts whenever I touch my scalp.
It started gradually about two weeks ago and has been steadily getting worse every day. It was not a sudden thunderclap pain.
It has been constant every single day for the past two weeks. I have never had a headache like this before in my entire life.
It is focused strictly on the right side of my head, right along my right temple.
It feels like a deep, persistent ache with a throbbing beat, and I would rate it an 8 out of 10 in severity.
The throbbing ache is there all day and night. It does not particularly wake me from sleep, but it never really goes away.
Touching my right temple makes it worse, and lying down or coughing does not change it. Nothing has really made it feel better.
Yes, my scalp is extremely tender on the right side. It hurts quite a bit even just brushing or combing my hair.
Yes, whenever I chew firm food like steak or hard bread, my jaw muscles cramp up, get exhausted, and hurt until I stop chewing.
Yesterday, the vision in my right eye went completely dark for about two minutes, like a black curtain falling over it, and then slowly came back.
No, I didn't see any flashing lights, zigzag lines, or tingling before the headache started.
I have felt slightly sick to my stomach from the severe pain, but I haven't thrown up. Light and loud sounds do not bother me.
No, I haven't had any eye redness, tearing, runny nose, or drooping of my eyelid.
I felt a bit warm and tired lately, but I haven't measured a high fever, and my neck moves without any stiffness.
No, I haven't had any numbness, weakness in my face or arms, slurred speech, or confusion.
I have had chronic stiffness and aching in both shoulders and hips in the morning, which my doctor told me was polymyalgia rheumatica.
No, I haven't bumped my head or suffered any falls or head injuries recently.
I tried taking over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen a few times, but they barely took the edge off.
No, I have been sleeping normally and haven't had any unusual food, alcohol, or sudden stress.
No, nobody else in my home has a headache, and our heating system is electric and working fine.
No, I do not have high blood pressure, and I do not take any blood thinners or aspirin.
No, I have never had cancer, and I do not have HIV or take any immune-weakening drugs.
Since it's on one side of my head and throbbing, I was wondering if it might be a migraine.
I am terrified that the temporary blindness from yesterday will happen again and that I might go permanently blind.
I was hoping you could order an MRI of my head to see what is going on inside.
I was diagnosed with polymyalgia rheumatica about a year ago. Otherwise, I've generally been healthy.
I had a gallbladder removal surgery about twenty years ago without any problems, and no other surgeries or hospital stays.
I am not currently taking any prescription medications. I completed a course of steroids for my polymyalgia a few months ago.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only have an occasional glass of wine at family gatherings on holidays, nothing regular.
I am a retired school teacher and live comfortably with my husband in a single-story house.
There is no history of aneurysms, brain tumors, or severe chronic headaches in my family. Both my parents lived into their eighties.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 138/84 mmHg, pulse 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 37.1 C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.

Visual acuity is 20/25 in both eyes, pupils are equal and reactive without afferent pupillary defect, visual fields are full, and fundus examination reveals crisp optic disc margins without pallor or swelling.
The right temporal artery is visibly prominent, firm, nodular, tender to palpation, and lacks a palpable pulse, while other peripheral pulses are normal.
No tenderness over the frontal or maxillary sinuses bilaterally.
The neck is supple with full range of motion; Kernig and Brudzinski signs are absent.
Cranial nerves II through XII are intact, facial sensation is normal and symmetric, and facial motor movements are symmetrical.
Motor strength is 5/5 in all four extremities with normal muscle tone and bulk.
Normal light touch, pinprick, and vibration sensation bilaterally.
Normal finger-to-nose testing, normal rapid alternating movements, and a steady, non-ataxic gait.
Temporomandibular joints have full range of motion without clicking, and shoulder joints show no swelling or warmth with mild non-tender stiffness.
